title: São Paulo Beats Inter and Ends Fan Protest
seoTitle: São Paulo beats Inter, fan protest ends
subtitle: Number 9 converts penalty at 14 minutes, and the crowd resumes chanting after 15-minute protest
excerpt: In a match valid for the 28th round of the Brasileirão, São Paulo defeated Internacional 1-0 at Morumbi, while organized fans staged a silent protest.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The clash between São Paulo and Internacional, valid for the 28th round of the Brazilian Championship, ended with a 1-0 victory for the Tricolor and was highlighted by organized fans staging a silent protest during the first 15 minutes of the game.

Organized Fan Protest

For the first fourteen minutes of the match, the Tricolor's main organized fan groups remained silent, following a decision by a leader known as Baby, who explained that the silence would be maintained so as not to startle the athletes. The measure was taken after Dorival Júnior's statement about the players' anxiety following their elimination in the Copa Sudamericana quarterfinals.

Calleri's Penalty Goal

The silence was broken when, at 14 minutes, the referee awarded a penalty after Maripán's fall on the number 10. Luciano stepped up to take the kick, but it was Calleri who converted, putting São Paulo ahead. The goal occurred before the resumption of fan chants, which only reactivated after the 15-minute protest was completed.

Starters' Performance

São Paulo saw the debut of Pedro Lima, who started and was substituted in the second half. Domingos Duarte felt discomfort and left the field, making way for Sabino. On Inter's side, reserve goalkeeper Anthoni came in after Matheus Cunha showed flu-like symptoms.

League Standings

With the victory, the Tricolor now has 36 points, placing them five points above the relegation zone and in 11th position. Internacional remains in 18th place with 28 points, having played one more game than Grêmio.

Upcoming Fixtures

After the match, São Paulo has a break until their next clash against Santos, scheduled for October 2nd. Inter returns to the field on the 7th, facing Corinthians.

With information from UOL, ge.
